nodes.title: Dataverse plug-ins: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A plug-in is custom .NET code registered against the Dataverse event pipeline — it runs when a row is created, updated, deleted, or another message fires. Plug-ins are the core server-side extensibility model tested on PL-400.

flashcards.front: What are the stages of the event pipeline?
flashcards.back: Pre-validation (outside the transaction), pre-operation (in transaction, before the main operation), and post-operation (in transaction, after). Pre stages can change input values; post stages react to the committed result. Choosing the right stage is a common exam point.

Synchronous runs inline and can block/roll back the operation — use it when the user must see the effect immediately or you must veto the change. Asynchronous runs later via the system job queue — use it for slow or non-critical work so the user isn't kept waiting.

Plug-ins run in a partial-trust sandbox: no file system, no most native calls, and only outbound HTTP/HTTPS allowed. It's required for cloud and enforces security and tenant isolation. Design plug-ins to stay within these limits.

flashcards.front: How do you pass data into a plug-in?
flashcards.back: The execution context carries InputParameters (the Target entity/reference), pre- and post-images (snapshots of the row before/after), shared variables, and the user context. Register only the images and attributes you need to keep performance up.

questions.q: A developer is registering a synchronous plug-in that must roll the database write back if it raises an exception, and the logic depends on values the user just typed but that have not yet been committed to the table. Which step of the Dataverse event execution pipeline should the plug-in be registered on?
choices: PreValidation — runs outside the database transaction, so any exception it throws will not roll the transaction back
PreOperation — runs inside the database transaction and before the core operation, so exceptions roll the transaction back and the Target entity still carries the uncommitted attribute values
PostOperation — runs after the core operation, so the attribute values have already been written and a thrown exception only logs an error
MainOperation — the core platform operation itself, which custom plug-ins cannot be registered against
questions.explanation: The Dataverse event pipeline has four stages: PreValidation (10, outside the database transaction), PreOperation (20, inside the transaction and before the core write), MainOperation (30, reserved for the platform), and PostOperation (40, inside the transaction and after the core write). For a plug-in that needs both transactional rollback on failure and access to uncommitted values from the Target, PreOperation is the right stage — PreValidation is outside the transaction so it cannot roll back, PostOperation runs after the write has already happened, and MainOperation is reserved for the platform.

questions.q: A maker requires that whenever an Opportunity is set to Won, the related Account's Credit Limit is increased by a percentage that depends on the deal value, the change must be transactional with the Opportunity update, and the rule must run regardless of whether the change is made from a model-driven app, a canvas app, a flow, or the Web API. Which automation should the developer build?
choices: A Dataverse business rule scoped to All Forms, with an If/Then action that updates the Account
A canvas app Power Fx formula on the Opportunity edit screen's OnSave property
A scheduled cloud flow that runs every 15 minutes, queries Won opportunities, and updates accounts
A synchronous Dataverse plug-in registered on the Update message of Opportunity in the PostOperation stage, filtered to the StateCode attribute
questions.explanation: When the rule has to fire on every channel that writes to Dataverse (UI, Power Automate, Web API, integrations) and has to be transactional with the source write, the right tool is a synchronous plug-in on the Update message in the PostOperation stage, with the filtering attribute set to StateCode so the plug-in only runs when the status changes. Business rules are evaluated client-side on forms (and only partially server-side) so they will not fire from many channels and cannot perform cross-table updates with this kind of logic. Power Fx OnSave only fires in that canvas app. A scheduled flow is not transactional and introduces a delay.

questions.q: A plug-in must call an external HTTPS API and parse the JSON response. The developer notices that calls work in unit tests but fail when the plug-in is deployed and registered in isolation (sandbox) mode. What is the correct understanding of the sandbox restriction?
choices: The sandbox blocks all outbound HTTP traffic; isolation must be set to None and the assembly stored on disk for any external call to succeed
The sandbox blocks access to local disk and the registry but permits outbound HTTPS calls; the failure is therefore caused by the assembly being too large to load
The sandbox runs in full trust; the failure is caused by missing System.Net.Http references that must be added via NuGet at registration time

The sandbox blocks access to the file system, the registry, certain reflection, and other system resources, but does permit outbound HTTP/HTTPS calls — failures are usually authentication, allow-listed-port (80/443/HTTPS-only), or response-time related, not the network call itself
questions.explanation: All plug-ins in Dataverse must run in the sandbox (isolation mode = Sandbox); 'None' is not supported in online environments. The sandbox blocks access to the file system, the registry, parts of reflection, system event logs, and a few other resources, but it does permit outbound HTTP and HTTPS calls on the standard ports, with a two-minute execution limit per call. So a failing external call is almost always due to authentication, network egress restrictions on the target side, port restrictions, exceeding the time limit, or unhandled exceptions — not the network call itself being blocked. None-isolation and on-disk assemblies are not options online, and the sandbox is not full-trust.

questions.q: A plug-in must run AFTER an Account is created and the database transaction has committed, to call an external billing API. Registering it in the pre-operation or post-operation synchronous stages risks rolling back the transaction if the API is slow. What is the correct registration?
choices: Synchronous, pre-validation stage, so the external billing API is invoked before any database work for the Account create begins at all
Asynchronous, post-operation stage, so it runs after the transaction commits without blocking it
Synchronous, post-operation stage, with a long timeout to accommodate the external call
A real-time workflow on create, since workflows cannot affect plug-in transactions
questions.explanation: Asynchronous post-operation plug-ins execute outside the main transaction after commit via the async service — the external call can't roll back the Account create and won't block the user. Synchronous stages (pre-validation, pre/post-operation) run inside the transaction, so a slow API delays or rolls it back; a real-time workflow is also synchronous and carries the same risk.

questions.q: In a plug-in's pre-operation Update step, a developer needs the value a field held BEFORE the update to compare against the new value. Which property of the execution context provides the prior value?
choices: InputParameters["Target"], which always carries the complete record including unchanged fields
PostEntityImages, captured automatically for every registered Update step at runtime
PreEntityImages, when a pre-image was registered on the step for the needed attributes
SharedVariables, where the platform stores the prior field values for plug-in chains
questions.explanation: A registered pre-image snapshots specified attributes as they were before the operation; the plug-in reads PreEntityImages to get old values. The Target only contains the attributes being changed (not unchanged ones, and showing new values); post-images hold after-values; SharedVariables pass data between plug-ins, not field history.

nodes.title: Mixed exam topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Some exam objectives don't fit neatly into a single domain — they span protocols, tools, or concepts covered briefly in multiple sections. These cards treat each item as a stand-alone fact, the way an exam question presents it: one concept, one answer.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a hub, a switch, and a router?
flashcards.back: Hub: Layer 1, repeats every frame to all ports — all devices share bandwidth, collisions guaranteed. Switch: Layer 2, forwards frames using a MAC address table to only the destination port — full duplex, no collisions, each port gets full bandwidth. Router: Layer 3, makes forwarding decisions based on IP address, connects different networks. Hub is legacy; switches dominate LAN; routers are at network edges.

flashcards.front: What is RAID 5 and how many drives can it tolerate losing?
flashcards.back: RAID 5 stripes data and parity across at least 3 drives. Any single drive failure can be recovered by reconstructing missing data from the remaining drives and parity. It cannot tolerate 2 simultaneous drive failures. Effective capacity = (N-1) × drive size. Read performance is excellent; write requires parity recalculation. RAID 6 tolerates 2 failures using double parity.

flashcards.front: What does a proxy server do, and how does a forward proxy differ from a reverse proxy?
flashcards.back: Forward proxy: sits between clients and the internet on behalf of clients — used for content filtering, caching, and anonymizing outbound requests (the server sees the proxy's IP). Reverse proxy: sits in front of servers on behalf of the server — used for load balancing, SSL termination, caching, and hiding backend topology (the client sees the proxy's IP). Both intermediate HTTP, but they protect opposite sides.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of a DMZ in network architecture?
flashcards.back: A demilitarized zone is a network segment between the untrusted internet and the trusted internal network, typically protected by two firewalls (or two interfaces on one firewall). Public-facing services (web, email, DNS) sit in the DMZ: internet can reach them but not the internal network; if the DMZ host is compromised, the inner firewall still blocks access to the internal LAN.

questions.q: A team needs a reusable star-rating control that runs inside both model-driven app forms and canvas apps, displays bound numeric data from a Dataverse column, and ships through the standard solution layering process. Which Power Platform technology should they build?
choices: A JavaScript web resource attached to the form's OnLoad event using Xrm.Page
A Power Apps canvas component library shared from a single canvas app
A Power Apps Component Framework (PCF) code component built with the pcf-scripts CLI
A custom HTML web resource embedded in an iframe on the form
questions.explanation: The Power Apps Component Framework (PCF) is purpose-built for reusable, data-bound UI controls that work in model-driven forms, views, dashboards, and canvas apps. PCF components are authored with the pcf-scripts CLI (npm package), packaged into a solution, and bound to Dataverse columns through a manifest. JavaScript web resources can attach script to forms but do not produce a packaged, reusable control; canvas component libraries only work inside canvas apps; HTML web resources in iframes cannot be data-bound to a column and are not reusable across app types.

questions.q: A Power Apps component framework (PCF) code component must read and write the bound column's value on the form. Which lifecycle method supplies the latest context (and is where the control should request a re-render of changed values)?
choices: init, which fires once and holds the only reference to the bound value for the control's lifetime
updateView, called by the framework whenever bound data or context changes
getOutputs, which the framework polls continuously to push values back to the form
destroy, where the current value must be cached before the control is torn down
questions.explanation: updateView receives the refreshed context each time bound properties or layout change — the control reads current values there and updates its UI. init runs once for setup; getOutputs returns changed values back to the host (called after notifyOutputChanged), it isn't a polling source of inputs; destroy is cleanup only.

questions.q: A developer needs to expose a third-party REST API that uses OAuth 2.0 client credentials to every maker in the tenant so it can be used from Power Apps and Power Automate. They already have the OpenAPI 2.0 definition. What is the most appropriate object to create?
choices: A custom connector, registered with the OpenAPI definition, configured with the OAuth 2.0 client credentials authentication type, and shared with the organization
A Dataverse virtual table that points at the REST endpoint with a custom data provider plug-in
An on-premises data gateway pointing at the REST endpoint so connector traffic is proxied through it
A Power Automate child flow that wraps the REST call and is published as a managed solution
questions.explanation: Custom connectors are the canonical wrapper for REST APIs in Power Platform: import the OpenAPI (Swagger) definition, choose an authentication type (OAuth 2.0, API key, Basic, Microsoft Entra ID, generic OAuth, etc.), define triggers/actions, then share the connector with users or the entire organization. Virtual tables are for surfacing external data as Dataverse rows, not for action-style API calls. On-premises gateways are for on-prem data sources, not Internet-reachable REST APIs. Child flows wrap reusable Power Automate logic but do not expose the API itself as a first-class connector to other apps.

questions.q: A solution architect must choose between a canvas app and a model-driven app. The requirements are: a strongly opinionated record-centric UI generated from a Dataverse table's forms and views, role-based security driven by Dataverse security roles, and standard business process flows on each record. Which app type fits, and why?
choices: Model-driven — the UI is generated from the table's forms, views, charts, and dashboards, and security flows directly from the user's Dataverse security roles assigned in the environment
Canvas — canvas apps natively render Dataverse forms and views and inherit Dataverse security roles without any extra configuration
Power Pages — Power Pages is the only Power Apps surface that ships record-centric forms with security roles
Power BI embedded app — Power BI apps host Dataverse forms and provide Dataverse security automatically
questions.explanation: Model-driven apps are designed around data: you compose them by picking tables, forms, views, charts, dashboards, and business process flows; the platform renders the UI for you, and security is enforced by the user's Dataverse security roles in the environment. Canvas apps give pixel-level layout control but do not 'render' a Dataverse table's forms and views — you build screens manually. Power Pages is the rebrand of Portals, a public-facing website, not the internal app surface described. Power BI is analytics, not a transactional app builder.

questions.q: A developer needs to retrieve the top 50 active contacts from a custom Web API client, returning only the fullname and emailaddress1 columns, ordered by createdon descending. Which Dataverse Web API URL is correctly formed?
choices: GET /api/data/v9.2/contacts?filter=statecode=0&select=fullname,emailaddress1&orderby=createdon desc&top=50
GET /api/data/v9.2/contacts?$select=fullname,emailaddress1&$filter=statecode eq 0&$orderby=createdon desc&$top=50
GET /api/data/v9.2/contacts/query?columns=fullname,emailaddress1&where=statecode=0&order=createdon DESC&limit=50
POST /api/data/v9.2/RetrieveMultiple with a JSON body listing the table, columns, filter, sort, and page size
questions.explanation: The Dataverse Web API is an OData v4 endpoint, so query options are prefixed with a dollar sign — $select, $filter, $orderby, $top — and the filter uses OData operators such as `eq`, not SQL `=`. Plural entity-set names (contacts, accounts) address the collection. The other options use SQL-style or invented syntax. RetrieveMultiple is the old Organization Service (SOAP) method name and is not a Web API route.

questions.q: An administrator wants users in a regional team to read and write only the records owned by users in their own business unit, while a corporate analyst role reads every record in the organization but writes none. Which two Dataverse security concepts together model this?
choices: Field-level security profiles on the Owner column, combined with model-driven app sharing rules per business unit
Environment-level conditional access policies in Microsoft Entra ID, combined with Dataverse hierarchical security

Security roles with privileges set at the appropriate access level — Business Unit for the regional read/write, Organization for the corporate read — assigned to users alongside their business unit membership
Sharing each record individually with the relevant team via the Share command on the form
questions.explanation: Dataverse security combines business units (a hierarchy users belong to) with security roles (which list privileges per table and an access level — User, Business Unit, Parent: Child Business Unit, or Organization). To grant read/write inside the user's own business unit you give Read and Write at the Business Unit level on those tables; to grant org-wide read-only you give Read at the Organization level and no Create/Write privilege. Field-level security restricts which columns a user can see, not which rows. Conditional access governs sign-in, not Dataverse row scope. Manual sharing is per record and does not scale.

questions.q: A developer is wiring a Power Automate cloud flow that must fire as soon as any row in the Dataverse Case table is created OR updated, but only when the case priority is High. The same flow should not run for every column change. Which trigger configuration is correct?
choices: Use two separate flows — one with the When a row is added trigger and one with the When a row is modified trigger — and copy the action steps between them
Use the When a row is added, modified, or deleted (Dataverse) trigger, set Change type to Added or Modified, leave Select columns empty, and add a Condition action inside the flow to check priority
Use a recurrence trigger that runs every minute and queries Cases with priority=High created or modified in the last minute

Use the When a row is added, modified, or deleted (Dataverse) trigger, set Change type to Added or Modified, set Filter rows to `prioritycode eq 1`, and list the priority and relevant columns under Select columns
questions.explanation: The When a row is added, modified, or deleted Dataverse trigger supports server-side filtering and column scoping, which keeps flow runs and API consumption down. Change type chooses Added/Modified. Filter rows takes an OData expression (`prioritycode eq 1` for High) so the trigger fires only on matching rows. Select columns lists the trigger columns so updates to other columns do not fire the flow. Two separate flows duplicate maintenance and miss the column-scope optimization. An in-flow Condition wastes a run for every Case change. Polling every minute is expensive and misses near-real-time changes.

questions.q: A team has built a solution in their development environment containing a custom table, two model-driven apps, and a plug-in assembly. They want to deploy it to test and production in a way that prevents target-environment makers from modifying its components and supports clean uninstall. Which solution type should they export?
choices: A managed solution — components are locked against editing in the target environment, dependencies are tracked, and uninstalling the solution removes its components cleanly
An unmanaged solution — required for production because only unmanaged solutions can be updated by future development releases
A patch on the unmanaged base — patches are the supported deployment artifact for non-development environments
A solution package exported as a .csproj with the Solution Packager only — managed/unmanaged is a development-time concept that does not affect target environments
questions.explanation: Managed solutions are the canonical ALM artifact for non-development environments: components are read-only to target-environment users, dependencies are enforced, and uninstalling the managed solution removes its components. Unmanaged solutions are containers used during development; importing them into production lets anyone modify the components and there is no clean uninstall. Patches are an optional layering mechanism on top of a managed base, not a replacement for managed deployment. Solution Packager is a tooling option for source control, not a substitute for the managed/unmanaged distinction.
